selection_rule: Prefer externally demonstrated mechanisms that are executable with existing capability, have a clear payment boundary, and can produce independent evidence without copying protected implementation.

lanes.primitive: verify identity/authorization/claim -> collect evidence -> issue bounded verdict -> retain evidence receipt
lanes.next_test: Map one existing supplier-verification offer to a deterministic evidence contract. No external activation.

lanes.primitive: collect supplier inputs -> normalize price/terms -> reconcile differences -> produce attributable comparison artifact
lanes.next_test: Define acceptance criteria and required evidence for one bounded comparison. No external activation.

lanes.primitive: settled payment/authorized entitlement -> issue license identifier -> bind entitlement to deliverable -> retain issuance evidence
lanes.next_test: Determine whether license issuance can be added without new paid infrastructure or weakening attribution.

lanes.primitive: detect exception -> classify -> propose authorized action -> execute only when gated -> record outcome
lanes.next_test: Find an existing paid, fulfillable exception-resolution use case before building anything.

proof_bound_commerce_anchor.rule: Payment observation never equals completed economic outcome. Verification requires attributable buyer evidence, settled payment, fulfillment, and independent proof.

hard_boundaries: No proprietary code or confidential implementation copying
No public outreach without human authorization
No revenue recognition from internal events
